about: The first simulated pool on testnet (ops/deploy_sim.py pool): a menu of 5 000 for 45 and 10 000 for 85 USDC, so 1 600 locked (two payouts of 800). Both stages: target 10 %, drawdown 6 % from the start, daily loss 3 % from the day's snapshot, leverage by the rule v1.3. Thirty days a stage, and max_idle_s the same thirty days: the factory needs it set, and set to the stage's length it never ends a stage before its deadline, so the terms name no idle rule. A fill costs 450 ppm, Hyperliquid's taker fee, with no builder fee: nothing here trades on the exchange. Fills at the book, at most 150 bp worse than the oracle (testnet's books stood 77 to 118 bp off it on 11 November 2026). fill_window: 10 blocks until the keeper's --measure gives the number.
terms_text: Simulated pool, testnet. Both stages are paper exams on nobody's money; prices are testnet USDC. An exam costs the price of its line: 5 000 for 45, 10 000 for 85. Each stage: profit target 10 % of the size, no more than 6 % below the starting balance, no more than 3 % below the day's first snapshot (equity with open profit, taken in the first minutes of the UTC day), leverage at most 10x on BTC and ETH and 5x on SOL, thirty days at most, with no minimum of trading days. A fill takes the book's price, never better than the oracle's and at most 1.5 % worse, and pays 0.045 % of its notional, Hyperliquid's taker fee. Whoever passes the exam starts the stage within seven days; whoever passes the stage is paid 8 % of the size, once, 48 hours later, unless the platform's checker stops it before then with a reason written on chain: opposite positions with another account of the platform, or that and wallets linked. A stopped payout's money stays in the pool. The platform takes 0.5 % of each price and of each withdrawal, and 1 HYPE to open the pool.
